items.title: At some point, not knowing becomes a choice
items.excerpt: Open the retro notes from a year ago. Then open last quarter's. The same problem is in both, in almost the same words. The dependency that strangles every release. The hand-off that loses a week. The "we should really talk about the roadmap" that never becomes a conversation. It's been named, written down, and nodded at, four times now, by the same people, who will name it again next quarter and nod again. That's the moment this rule is about. Not the problem. The nodding. Because at some point, a problem that keeps getting raised and never gets fixed stops being a problem the organization has

items.title: From Past Me to Future Us
items.excerpt: I deliberately make tiny investments in learning opportunities for me and my colleagues. Yesterday I was reviewing a PR which had a large number of edits to data using a few patterns applied in many places. Unfortunately, the edits were embedded in non-trivial contexts which made the diffs less easy to eyeball than I might have hoped. Here's an invented example that gives a flavour of the problem. The first line is an original, the second an edit: - (ab)38458345023421-5-7345234D + (ab)038458345023421-5-7345234 $ git diff | grep "^- " | sed 's/(ab)3/(ab)03/' | sed 's/D$//' | sed 's/-/+/' > mych
